# incomplete fixtures

Half-typed input. For each `*.rsx` the parser must return an AST with error nodes (never panic), and recovery-mode codegen must emit Rust in which every complete Rust expression is still analyzable by rust-analyzer. These three are required for Gate 1.

Each `*.rsx` also has a sibling `*.expected` listing the Outou diagnostics it must produce, verbatim and in the order the parser emits them (innermost construct first), in the same format as `tests/fixtures/diagnostics/`. Rust-level errors from blocks the parser closes implicitly at end of input are not listed, except for an unclosed function body cut at the next item, which is always listed (``unclosed body of function …``, `docs/grammar.md` §9). These files are whole mid-edit buffers: a trailing `}` that closes the enclosing `fn` is part of what recovery must handle (`docs/grammar.md` §2.2).

The `*-mid-file` fixtures (a `fn Before` above, a `fn After` below; `bodyless-fn-mid-file`, `class-attribute-value-mid-file`, `unclosed-island-mid-file`, `unclosed-tag-mid-file`) also pin the swallowed-tail fix: `fn After` must survive as its own item (`swallowed_tail_fixtures_keep_the_item_after_the_broken_construct` in `crates/outou-backend-dioxus/tests/recovery.rs`). `fragment-truncated-closing-tag-eof` (a truncated `</` after the children of an unclosed `<>`) and `stray-truncated-closing-tag-eof` (a top-level `</div` at end of file) pin the truncated-closing-tag shapes of a fragment and of `recover_stray_close`. `fragment-unclosed-in-element`, `fragment-with-unclosed-child` and `fragment-unclosed-mid-file` (fragment as the open element, ADR 0015) pin that an unclosed `<>` reports ``missing closing tag `</>` `` once and, mid-file, leaves `fn After` alone. The `stray-closing-tag-interrupted-by-{rbrace,lt}` and `fragment-closing-tag-interrupted-by-{rbrace,lt}` fixtures pin the `}`- and `<`-interrupted shapes of the same two recoveries (a `<` that starts JSX is consumed into the recovery element so Recovery output stays valid Rust).

`attribute-value-missing-before-sibling` (`<div class=` followed by a sibling element) pins issue #19: the sibling survives as its own element instead of becoming attributes of the broken tag, which is what lets `outou-lsp`'s completion classify the cursor.
